nodes.summary: Martin proved in ZFC that every Borel game is determined, the strongest determinacy statement ZFC proves; the proof needs the axiom of replacement. Determinacy of analytic games needs more: Martin derived it from a measurable cardinal. Projective determinacy follows from infinitely many Woodin cardinals (Martin and Steel, 1989), which this graph does not yet define.
nodes.title: Borel and analytic determinacy

nodes.summary: Two players alternately choose moves `x 0, x 1, x 2, …` from a set `A`, each seeing all earlier moves; player I wins if the play lies in the payoff set `S ⊆ A^ℕ`. A strategy maps finite histories to moves, and `S` is determined if one player has a winning strategy. The Gale–Stewart theorem says that open and closed payoff sets are determined; every later determinacy proof (Martin's for Borel sets, Martin–Steel's…
nodes.title: Gale–Stewart games

nodes.summary: With the axiom of choice, some game on `{0, 1}` is not determined (Gale and Stewart, 1953): a diagonalisation over the continuum many strategies, each of which has continuum many plays. Hence the axiom of determinacy, that every subset of Baire space is determined, is false in Lean's ambient logic; results "under AD" are stated with determinacy hypotheses on specific classes of sets instead.
nodes.title: Non-determined games

nodes.summary: If every set in a reasonable class of sets of reals is determined, every set in the class is regular: it is countable or contains a perfect set (Davis), it has the property of Baire (Banach–Mazur, Oxtoby), and it is measurable for every σ-finite Borel measure (Mycielski–Świerczkowski). nodes.title: Regularity of sets of reals from determinacy
